normalized_r_metric: 1R=initial stop price distance; each trade treated as equal nominal initial R (fractional lots implicit), net R includes assumed cost relative to that trade's stop
methodology: OHLC replay next-open fill, stop first on same OHLC bar, worse gaps, 1/3 at 1R, 1/3 at 1.5R, runner; baseline original engine, BE original engine; ATR2 trail based only on last closed ATR and previous 3 bars after TP2; time 24h exits at open; all same 96-trading-hour quarter embargo
technical_findings: R-normalized net after US$1.2 cost reveals ShockExhaustion M5 2025 -20.499R despite +10394.8 POINTS, so raw point profit can conceal negative constant-risk expectancy.
R-normalized net after US$1.2 cost reveals EMA21+RSI+MACD M30 2025 -10.011R despite +7720.5 POINTS.
Unmodified ER20 M30 remains positive +23.729R in 2025, +11.623R in partial 2026 under assumed cost1.2.
Unmodified ShockExhaustion M15 remains positive +27.857R in 2025 and +11.682R in partial 2026, but insufficient historical samples 90/45 under fixed 100/50 trade threshold.
Zero alternative exit variant improved R net in BOTH periods, and none met preregistered simultaneous improvement + cost + risk constraints.

Early 24-hour exit and ATR trailing frequently increased trade count and worsened net, likely by limiting winners and changing entry availability; no proof which mechanism dominates without per-trade attribution.
Do not change any user-selected archived strategies or live trading because the research did not validate a superior exit.
known_limits: 2025 and 2026 data previously repeatedly inspected; no fresh out-of-sample and 2026 only partial.
Different exits change trade counts through position availability; results are full-policy comparisons not matched-only-trade treatment effects.
R normalization assumes divisible positions and no lot rounding; not an executable portfolio or percentage return.
No true broker ticks/Bid-Ask, commissions, swap, slippage, dynamic spread, margin, capital allocation, intratrade equity max drawdown.
